tasha: heads-up — canary bring-up for cygnus-13b (int4) is showing two problems: intermittent OOMs when batch_size >= 2 and a small but consistent quality regression on long-context summarization prompts. dumping quick notes below.

ben_runtime: can you paste the route defaults and a failing log snippet?

morgan_ml: quick thought — int4 can magnify frag issues if max_new_tokens is large by default. what are we using?

Tasha: route defaults for the canary: 
```
model: cygnus-13b-int4
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_size: 8
  max_batch_wait_ms: 12
defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 256
  temperature: 0.7
  session_kv_enabled: true
```
example client call: `POST /v1/generate {"model":"cygnus-13b-int4","input":"<long doc>","max_new_tokens":256}`

failing log (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-21 17:10:03] ERROR serve/runtime: allocation failed: cudaMalloc returned 2 (out of memory)
[2026-03-21 17:10:03] WARN runtime/memory: fragmentation ratio 0.78, largest_free 452MB
[2026-03-21 17:10:04] INFO batching: batch_size=3, token_budget=1024
```

diego_infra: fragmentation ratio ~0.78 is suspicious. likely slot churn from large KV cache + variable sequence lengths. two immediate mitigations: 1) lower route default max_new_tokens to reduce KV growth, 2) enable periodic slot compaction on idle GPUs (we can do a soft compaction between canary runs).

ben_runtime: agree. also consider gating batching when the active sequence length distribution exceeds X. i.e. microbatch when avg_seq_len > 512. simple policy patch we can try:
```
batching.policies:
- name: seq_len_gate
  if: avg_input_tokens > 512
  action: force_microbatch
  microbatch_size: 1
```

morgan_ml: for the quality regression — dropping to int4 changed logit scaling on rare tokens. i recommend a two-pronged approach: 1) reduce default max_new_tokens to 64 for canary to limit KV and also reduce surface area for generation drift; 2) run a small quant-PTQ recalibration on the attention out projection for the last 6 layers (cheap) and run eval harness.

eval-bot: quick canary eval results (baseline FP16 vs canary int4):
- 200 QA pairs (long doc summaries): FP16 acc 82.5% | int4 acc 78.9% (delta -3.6pp)
- P95 latency: FP16 420ms | int4 360ms
- Failure (OOM) rate observed on canary traffic: 0.9% (mostly when batch_size>1 and prompts > 3k tokens)

tasha: good, actionable. ben/diego — can you propose the exact config diff we want to ship to the canary? i want minimal change to reduce risk.

ben_runtime: propose this minimal diff to the canary route config:
```
defaults.max_new_tokens: 64  # was 256
batching.max_batch_size: 2   # conservative, prevents 3+ batch OOMs
batching.policies:
  - name: seq_gate_small
    if: avg_input_tokens > 512
    action: force_microbatch
```
also add a soft-fallback to a low-memory variant (cygnus-13b-int4-slim) when memory pressure > 85%.

diego_infra: i can apply the config change and roll the canary now. i'll also enable a background compaction job on the nodes (runs when GPU util < 10% for 60s). patch to ops manifest: `enable_slot_compaction: true`

morgan_ml: i'll queue the light PTQ recalibration and run the eval harness against the canary after diego rolls. should take ~45m.

tasha: smoke test commands for when you finish the roll?

diego_infra: use these:
```
# smoke generation
curl -s -X POST $REDWOOD_API/v1/generate -d '{"model":"cygnus-13b-int4","input":"<test long doc>","max_new_tokens":60}' | jq '.status'
# run short eval (200 samples)
python infra/eval/run_eval.py --model cygnus-13b-int4 --suite long-doc-summary --count 200 --concurrency 4
```

ben_runtime: i'll also add a temporary metric alert: `canary_mem_pressure > 85% for 2m -> rollback` and `oom_rate > 0.5% for 10m -> rollback`

tasha: sounds good. tagging @morgan_ml to keep an eye on quality metrics. thanks everyone — i'll watch the canary dashboard and will post a short summary when the eval run completes. leaving smoke tests running now. :thumbsup:

eval-bot: scheduled eval started at 2026-03-21T17:22:00Z — ETA ~45m

tasha: leaving perf tests running, will report back in 2h.
